caption:
A soldier wakes on his funeral pyre.
A geologist falls from a mountain and watches his life unfold.
A physicist records the dying greeting the dead.

Plato. Albert Heim. Sir William Barrett.
Raymond Moody. Pim van Lommel.

Centuries apart. Different words.
The same pattern keeps returning.
Peace. Light. A life reviewed.
A border. A reluctance to come back.

In 2001, The Lancet published a prospective study.
344 hearts stopped.
62 came back with something to report.

Coincidence. A dying brain.
Or something that does not end when the body does.

The record is older than science.
The question remains open.

The full entry waits in the Forbidden Library: alloccult.com/consciousness/near-death-experiences

review_log.summary: Strong, accurate carousel with good images throughout. One blocking fix: slide 4. Barrett died in May 1925, so Death-Bed Visions was published posthumously in 1926, in London (Methuen), not Dublin. 'Physicist ... publishes' and 'Dublin · 1926' are therefore wrong, and the closing line is ungrammatical. Polish items: slide 6's 'crossing the threshold' overstates what the 62 patients reported, and the caption's 'The same tunnel' contradicts the archive page, which calls the tunnel culturally variable and often absent in Indian accounts.
fixes: slide 4 text: Barrett died in May 1925. Death-Bed Visions appeared posthumously in 1926 from Methuen in London, so 'publishes' and 'Dublin' are inaccurate. 'Some whose deaths no one had told them' is ungrammatical.

review_log.summary: The slides are accurate, well-illustrated and on-voice. Er's revival on the twelfth day, Heim's 1871 fall, the posthumous 1926 Death-Bed Visions and the Lancet figures of 344 patients and 62 NDEs all check out. One blocking issue: the caption claims these sources all share 'the same tunnel' and 'the same reluctance to return.' Heim, Er and Barrett's deathbed accounts report no tunnel, and the archive page itself calls the tunnel culturally variable. The caption needs a less absolute rewrite. Slide 6 has a minor wording polish.
fixes: caption: After naming Plato, Heim and Barrett, the caption claims 'the same tunnel' and 'the same reluctance to return.' Er, Heim and Barrett's deathbed accounts contain no tunnel, and the page itself says the tunnel is culturally variable and often absent. That is an overclaim a knowledgeable reader would reject. 'The Lancet published it' is also vague.

review_log.summary: Images all fit and are legible. Slides 1–5, 7 and 8 are accurate and on voice. One blocking problem remains on slide 6: van Lommel's 62 patients reported a near-death experience, not 'crossing the threshold.' In the Lancet paper only a small minority perceived a border, and none crossed one. The caption is fine after the round 2 fixes.
fixes: slide 6 text: Overclaim. In the 2001 Lancet study, 62 of 344 patients (18%) reported a near-death experience. Only a handful reported perceiving a border, and none 'crossed' one. A knowledgeable reader would call 'crossing the threshold' false. The page also specifies ten Dutch hospitals.

review_log.summary: Clean, accurate carousel. Er's twelfth-day revival on the pyre matches Republic X. Heim 1871, Barrett's posthumous 1926 Death-Bed Visions and the 2001 Lancet figures (344 patients, 62 NDEs, ten Dutch hospitals) are all correct. Every image is relevant, public domain and legible, and the earlier fixes hold. The only note is optional polish: the cover's 'Their stories match' slightly overstates the convergence the slides show. Ready to post.
